A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RF-AE research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, out-of-sample visualizations, a noisy artificial-tree experiment, and loss-weight and landmark-count ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results and visualizations, noise experiments, joint hyperparameter ablations, feature-importance sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: v1 uses KL reconstruction loss and PCA/k-means landmarks with probabilities summed over clusters. v3 Sections 3.2–3.3 replace these with Jensen–Shannon divergence and class-wise FasterPAM k-medoids prototypes, renormalizing probabilities over selected samples. These changes alter the objective, network inputs, and out-of-sample proximity computation, while retaining the overall RF-PHATE-regularized autoencoder framework.

E1.justification: v3 adds HAR, USPS, Blood MNIST, and OrganC MNIST, while removing Crowdsourced Mapping, White Wine Quality, and the reported Zilionis single-cell experiments. The artificial tree remains in the appendix with expanded noise conditions, although it leaves the benchmark dataset table. Coverage shifts materially toward activity recognition and biomedical images.

E2.justification: P-UMAP and PaCMAP enter the benchmark and visualization comparisons, while LOL is removed. Most comparators remain, including RF-PHATE (Ker.), renamed RF-PHATE. Encoder-only and unregularized RF-AE leave Table 1 but remain as the λ = 0 and λ = 1 ablations in v3 Tables 2 and S3.

E3.justification: Evaluation changes from k-NN-derived importances and ranks based on QNX/Spearman to ensemble-derived importances, four SIA metrics, and embedding classification accuracy. Neighborhood sizes change from 10–200 to 5–sqrt(Ntrain). Reported RF-AE batch size changes from 64 to 512, default λ from 0.001 to 0.01, and 2,000 landmarks to 10% prototypes. The noise experiment also changes its split and training budget.

E4.justification: The single-noise artificial-tree comparison becomes a multi-level SNR study with learning curves. Separate loss-weight and landmark studies become joint λ-by-prototype ablations. v3 adds pixel-importance analysis, alternative classification-importance strategies, and prototype timing experiments. OrganC case studies replace Zilionis analyses, and the additional MNIST qualitative case study is removed.

E5.justification: Ten repetitions were already reported in v1. v3 explicitly identifies different seeds and extends mean ± standard-deviation reporting to the central benchmark and ablations, beyond v1's rank-only main table and limited appendix uncertainty entries. New noise-learning curves show medians and 25th–75th percentiles across ten repetitions. The earlier Mann–Whitney landmark tests are removed.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 reports an average RF-AE rank of 4.38; v3 replaces that summary with new results, including 0.831 ± 0.011 classification accuracy and 0.776 ± 0.051 Spearman-based SIA. Classifier, OrganC, sensitivity, and runtime results are added, while Zilionis results disappear. Changed methods, datasets, and protocols prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 adds Appendix A's assumptions, Proposition A.1, proof, and finite-forest remarks, replacing v1's unconditional self-similarity assertion with a qualified asymptotic claim. Structural importance is also redefined as the drop from the unperturbed preservation score, whereas v1 Section 3.6 specifies the perturbed score itself. These are substantive formal changes.

C1.justification: The central claims of accurate, interpretable, robust out-of-sample supervised visualization remain. The introduction updates the scalability contribution from landmarks to prototypes, and the discussion now explicitly claims a better balance between informative-structure preservation and class separability, refining v1's emphasis on local/global structure preservation.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the KL-asymmetry explanation with a JSD-based rationale and attributes prototype benefits to implicit regularization and class-level denoising. It develops the structure-versus-separability interpretation and revises practical hyperparameter guidance. Organ-anatomy interpretations replace immune-lineage analyses, and the broader-impact discussion adds a specific proposed use for assessing diagnostic prediction reliability.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's existing architecture and optimizer details, v3 documents the importance-classifier implementations, model-specific baseline settings, GPU/CPU memory requirements, 1–6-hour experiment runtimes, and Hydra configuration management. It also announces code/configuration release and describes an anonymized supplementary zip. The PDFs alone do not establish actual access to those resources.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting JSD, f-divergences, prototype selection, FasterPAM, PaCMAP, and expanded evaluation metrics, while removing references associated with discarded comparisons and single-cell analyses. The main positioning relative to RF-PHATE, GRAE, and linear kernel extensions remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The methods exposition consolidates separate architecture, loss, and inference discussions. Evaluation and results are substantially rewritten around SIA and class separability. The appendices are reorganized into dedicated theory, evaluation, implementation, and analysis sections; the impact statement moves to an appendix, and a conference checklist is added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. Figure 1 is redrawn horizontally, Table 1 changes from ranks to five score columns, and Figure 2 replaces Zilionis with OrganC. New displays include importance heatmaps, noise-learning curves, joint ablation grids, and timing charts. Comparison grids and dataset tables are also redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical assessability: explicit SIA definitions, classifier-performance checks and alternative importance strategies address previously unexamined dependence on one evaluation proxy. Scores with dispersion, joint ablations, and timing measurements better substantiate quality, robustness, and efficiency claims; implementation and hardware details improve reproducibility. Single-cell evidence is lost, and Appendix A's cross-similarity rewrite omits the required out-of-bag indicator, so the added proof is not an unqualified gain. Nevertheless, the improved empirical validation and transparency provide a substantial net benefit.
